Enlarged basal part of carpel; contains ovules on placenta; develops into fruit after fertilisation

Carpels fused together in gynoecium; e.g., mustard, tomato
Arrangement of ovules (on placenta) within the ovary; marginal, axile, parietal, basal, free central

Placenta on central axis in multilocular ovary; e.g., china rose, tomato, lemon
Ovules on inner wall of unilocular ovary; e.g., mustard, Argemone

Placenta at base of ovary; single ovule; e.g., sunflower, marigold
Mature ripened ovary developed after fertilisation; pericarp + seeds
Fruit developing without fertilisation; no seeds; e.g., banana, some grapes

Middle layer of fleshy pericarp; fleshy edible part of mango; fibrous in coconut
Innermost layer of pericarp; stony hard layer of mango (surrounds seed)
Fleshy fruit with hard stony endocarp; one-seeded; from monocarpellary superior ovary; e.g., mango, coconut
Outer covering of seed; two layers: outer testa and inner tegmen
Outer layer of seed coat
Inner layer of seed coat
Scar on seed coat marking point of attachment of seed to fruit/funicle
Small pore in seed coat above hilum; site of water entry and pollen tube entry during fertilisation
Embryonic root in seed; develops into root system after germination
Embryonic shoot in seed; develops into shoot system after germination
Seed leaf; two in dicots (food storage), one (scutellum) in monocots
Central axis of embryo with radicle at one end and plumule at other end
Seed with endosperm persisting in mature seed; food stored in endosperm; e.g., castor, maize
Seed with no endosperm in mature stage; food stored in cotyledons; e.g., pea, bean, gram

Proteinous outermost layer of endosperm in maize; produces hydrolytic enzymes during germination
Sheath enclosing plumule in monocot seed; protects emerging shoot
Sheath enclosing radicle in monocot seed; protects emerging root
Symbolic representation of flower features showing number, arrangement, fusion and adhesion of floral parts
Diagrammatic cross-sectional representation of flower showing arrangement of all whorls
Study of internal structure of plants; shows similarities and differences not visible externally
Outermost tissue system; comprises epidermis, stomata, trichomes and root hairs; protective function
Outermost single layer of cells covering entire plant body; parenchymatous; bears cuticle, stomata, trichomes
Waxy thick layer on outside of epidermis; prevents water loss by transpiration; absent in roots
Pore in epidermis bounded by two guard cells; regulates transpiration and gaseous exchange; pl. stomata

Specialised epidermal cell surrounding guard cells; assists in stomatal movement
Stomatal pore + guard cells + subsidiary cells together
Multicellular epidermal hair on stem; may be branched, soft/stiff or secretory; reduces transpiration
All tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles; includes cortex, pericycle, pith; consists of parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma
Region between epidermis and stele (endodermis); parenchymatous; storage function
Outermost layer(s) of cortex just below epidermis; collenchymatous in dicot stem (support), sclerenchymatous in monocot stem
Innermost layer of cortex; single layer of barrel-shaped cells; has Casparian strips of suberin in roots; starch sheath in stems

All tissues inside endodermis: pericycle + vascular bundles + pith
Central parenchymatous tissue inside stele; food storage; large in monocot root; small in dicot root
Radially placed parenchymatous cells between vascular bundles in dicot stem; lateral conduction

Strand of xylem + phloem; open (with cambium, dicots) or closed (no cambium, monocots); radial or conjoint
Has cambium between xylem and phloem; can form secondary xylem and phloem; in dicot stems
No cambium; no secondary growth possible; in monocot stems
Xylem and phloem alternating along different radii; as in roots
Xylem and phloem on same radius; xylem inside, phloem outside; as in stems and leaves
Outermost layer (epidermis) of root; bears unicellular root hairs; no cuticle
Parenchymatous cells between xylem and phloem patches in root

Later-formed larger xylem; towards centre in roots; towards periphery in stems

Protoxylem towards periphery; characteristic of roots

Oval/round loosely arranged cells below palisade; large intercellular spaces; gas exchange

Monocot leaf; stomata on both surfaces; mesophyll not differentiated into palisade and spongy
Large empty colourless adaxial epidermal cell in grass leaves; when flaccid causes leaf rolling to reduce water loss
Simple tissue; thin-walled loosely packed cells with intercellular spaces; stores food; most abundant ground tissue
Simple tissue; unevenly thickened cellulose walls especially at corners; provides flexibility and mechanical support in young stems
Simple tissue; uniformly thick lignified dead cell walls; provides strength and rigidity; fibres and sclereids
Long narrow sclerenchyma cell; provides mechanical support; e.g., jute (Corchorus), hemp, flax
Short irregular-shaped sclerenchyma cell (stone cell); forms hard seed coat and gritty flesh of pear
Complex tissue; conducts water and minerals upward; made of tracheids, vessels, xylem parenchyma, xylem fibres
Elongated dead xylem cell with pitted walls; water conduction and support; present in all vascular plants
Wide, short dead xylem cell with perforated end walls; faster water conduction; only in angiosperms
Living xylem cells; store food and assist lateral water conduction
Complex tissue; conducts food (photosynthates) from leaves to rest of plant; sieve tubes, companion cells, phloem parenchyma, bast fibres
Living enucleate cell of phloem; sieve plates at ends for food flow; associated with companion cell
Nucleated cell adjacent to sieve tube element; controls metabolism of enucleate sieve tube
Perforated end wall of sieve tube element allowing food transport between cells
Actively dividing undifferentiated tissue; apical (root/shoot tip), lateral (cambium), intercalary (internodes)
Meristem at tips of roots and shoots; responsible for primary growth (increase in length)
Meristem on sides of organ; vascular cambium and cork cambium; responsible for secondary growth (increase in girth)
Meristem at internodes and leaf bases; responsible for growth of internodes; e.g., grasses
Lateral meristem between xylem and phloem; produces secondary xylem (inward) and secondary phloem (outward)
Secondary lateral meristem in bark; produces cork (phellem) outward and phelloderm inward
Dead suberised cells produced by cork cambium; replaces epidermis in older stems; waterproof
Pore in cork/bark for gaseous exchange when stomata are absent; in older stems and woody plants
Increase in girth due to activity of lateral meristems (vascular cambium + cork cambium); mostly in dicots
Dark dead inner wood; no water conduction; mechanically strong; tannins/resins deposited
Light outer wood; conducts water; living xylem; surrounds heartwood
Ring in wood cross-section from one year of secondary growth; spring wood (wide) + autumn wood (narrow)
Wide-pored, less dense wood formed in spring/summer; also called early wood
Narrow-pored, dense wood formed in autumn; also called late wood

Protective coloration allowing frogs to change colour to hide from predators (camouflage)
Summer sleep in frogs; shelter in deep burrows during peak summer to avoid extreme heat
Winter sleep in frogs; shelter in deep burrows during peak winter to avoid extreme cold
Transparent protective membrane covering frog's eye underwater
Membranous ear of frog on either side of eyes; receives sound signals
Males and females differ in external appearance; male frogs have vocal sacs and copulatory pad
Sound-producing organ in male frogs; absent in females
Gaseous exchange through moist skin; in frogs during aquatic phase and during aestivation/hibernation
Breathing using lungs; on land in frogs; air enters through nostrils → buccal cavity → lungs
Partially digested food passed from stomach to duodenum
Finger-like folds in inner wall of intestine; increase surface area for absorption of digested food
Tiny projections on villi; further increase surface area for absorption
Membrane covering the heart
Triangular structure joining right atrium of frog heart; receives blood from vena cava
Major veins bringing blood back to heart; open into sinus venosus
Sac-like chamber on ventral side of frog heart ventricle; blood exits to arteries
Venous connection between intestine and liver; brings absorbed nutrients to liver first
Venous connection between lower body and kidney; blood from hindlimbs filtered by kidney
System of lymph vessels and lymph nodes; lymph lacks proteins and RBCs; transports fats
Structural and functional unit of kidney (uriniferous tubule); filters blood and produces urine
Common duct for urine and sperm in male frogs; connects kidney/testis to cloaca
Excreting nitrogen mainly as urea; frog is ureotelic
Bony brain box enclosing and protecting brain; in all vertebrates
Anterior brain: olfactory lobes + cerebral hemispheres + diencephalon
Middle brain region; characterised by pair of optic lobes in frog
Posterior brain: cerebellum + medulla oblongata; medulla continues as spinal cord
Part of midbrain; processes visual information
Double fold of peritoneum attaching testes to kidneys in male frog
10-12 ducts from testis entering kidney and opening into Bidder's canal in male frog
Aquatic larval stage of frog; hatches from egg; undergoes metamorphosis to form adult
Transformation of tadpole larva into adult frog; involves reorganisation of body structures
Sheet-like animal tissue lining body surface and cavities; one free surface; protective and secretory
Animal tissue with cells in extracellular matrix; binds and supports other tissues; blood, bone, cartilage, areolar
Animal tissue composed of contractile cells (muscle fibres); skeletal, smooth and cardiac types
Nerve tissue made of neurons and neuroglia; generates and transmits electrical impulses

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: All living organisms are composed of cells; all cells arise from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula); formulated by Schleiden & Schwann, modified by Virchow (1855)

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Cell lacking membrane-bound nucleus and organelles; 70S ribosomes; bacteria, cyanobacteria, mycoplasma, PPLO

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Cell with membrane-bound nucleus and organelles; 80S cytoplasmic ribosomes; protists, fungi, plants, animals

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Semi-fluid matrix filling cell; main arena of cellular activities; contains organelles

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Selectively permeable bilayer of phospholipids and proteins; outer boundary of cell; fluid mosaic model

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Singer and Nicolson (1972): membrane is quasi-fluid phospholipid bilayer with laterally mobile integral and peripheral proteins

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Two layers of phospholipids with hydrophilic heads outward and hydrophobic tails inward; basic structure of cell membrane

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Protein partially or totally embedded in phospholipid bilayer; cannot be easily removed

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Protein lying on surface of membrane; loosely associated; easily removed

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Movement of molecules across membrane without energy; down concentration gradient; diffusion, osmosis, facilitated diffusion

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Energy-dependent (ATP) transport of molecules across membrane against concentration gradient; e.g., Na+/K+ pump

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Rigid non-living outer layer outside plasma membrane; in plants (cellulose), fungi (chitin), bacteria (peptidoglycan); gives shape and protection

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Thin, flexible cell wall of young/growing plant cell; capable of growth

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Thick, rigid wall formed inside primary wall of mature plant cell; contains lignin

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Layer of calcium pectate between adjacent cell walls; cements neighbouring plant cells together

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Cytoplasmic connections through cell wall linking neighbouring plant cells; allow cell-to-cell communication

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Multi-layered structure in bacteria: glycocalyx + cell wall + plasma membrane

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Outermost layer of bacterial cell envelope; loose slime layer or tough capsule; protection and adherence

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Tough, thick glycocalyx of certain bacteria; protects from phagocytosis and desiccation

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Infolding of bacterial plasma membrane; helps in cell wall formation, DNA replication, respiration and secretion

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Small circular DNA in bacteria outside genomic DNA; carries extra genes (e.g., antibiotic resistance)

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Elongated tubular protein projections on bacterial surface; help in attachment to surfaces and conjugation

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Small bristle-like protein fibres on bacteria; help attach to host tissues

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Thin filamentous extension for motility; composed of filament + hook + basal body; structurally different from eukaryotic flagellum

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Reserve material stored in prokaryotic cytoplasm without membrane; e.g., phosphate granules, glycogen granules, gas vacuoles

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Non-membrane-bound organelle; site of protein synthesis; 70S (prokaryotes) or 80S (eukaryotes)

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Chain of ribosomes attached to one mRNA molecule; translate same mRNA simultaneously

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Coordinated group of membrane organelles: ER + Golgi complex + lysosomes + vacuoles

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Network of tubules and cisternae in eukaryotic cytoplasm; RER (with ribosomes, protein synthesis) and SER (lipid synthesis)

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: ER with ribosomes on outer surface; site of protein synthesis and processing; continuous with outer nuclear membrane

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: ER without ribosomes; site of lipid and steroid hormone synthesis

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Stacked flattened membrane sacs (cisternae); cis face (receiving) and trans face (releasing); packages and modifies proteins; forms glycoproteins and glycolipids

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Flattened disc-shaped sacs of Golgi apparatus; 0.5–1.0 µm diameter; stacked parallel

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Membrane-bound vesicle containing hydrolytic enzymes (lipases, proteases, carbohydrases); active at acid pH; digests macromolecules; "suicide bag" of cell

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Membrane-bound space in cytoplasm; bound by tonoplast; stores water, sap, waste; up to 90% of plant cell volume

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Single membrane bounding the vacuole; facilitates transport of ions into vacuole against gradient

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Double-membrane organelle; site of aerobic respiration; produces ATP; has own 70S ribosomes and circular DNA; "powerhouse of cell"

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Infolding of inner mitochondrial membrane; increases surface area for ATP synthesis; pl. cristae

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Dense fluid inside inner mitochondrial membrane; site of Krebs cycle; contains circular DNA and 70S ribosomes

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Double-membrane plant organelle; chloroplasts (photosynthesis), chromoplasts (pigment), leucoplasts (storage)

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Green plastid containing chlorophyll; site of photosynthesis; thylakoids + stroma; has own 70S ribosomes and circular DNA

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Coloured (non-green) plastid containing carotenoids; gives yellow/orange/red colour to flowers and fruits

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Colourless plastid storing nutrients: amyloplasts (starch), elaioplasts (oils/fats), aleuroplasts (proteins)

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Fluid-filled matrix of chloroplast; site of Calvin cycle (dark reactions); contains circular DNA and 70S ribosomes

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Flattened membranous sac in chloroplast stroma; contains chlorophyll; stacked into grana; site of light reactions

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Stack of thylakoids in chloroplast; pl. grana; site of light reactions of photosynthesis

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Flat membranous tubule connecting thylakoids of different grana; intergranal thylakoid

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Network of microtubules, microfilaments, and intermediate filaments; provides mechanical support, shape, and motility to cell

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Hollow tube of tubulin protein; part of cytoskeleton; forms spindle fibres, cilia axoneme, centrioles

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Solid rod of actin protein; part of cytoskeleton; involved in cell movement and shape

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Short hair-like motile outgrowth of cell membrane; moves fluid past cell surface; 9+2 microtubule array; pl. cilia

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Long hair-like motile outgrowth for cell locomotion; 9+2 microtubule axoneme; structurally same as cilium but longer

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Core of cilium/flagellum; 9 peripheral doublet + 2 central microtubules (9+2 arrangement)

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Centriole-like structure at base of cilium/flagellum; anchors it in cell

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Non-membrane organelle in animal cells containing two centrioles; organises spindle fibres during cell division

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Cylindrical structure of 9 peripheral triplet microtubules; forms basal body of cilia/flagella and spindle apparatus

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Membrane-bound organelle containing chromosomes; controls cell activities and heredity; first described by Robert Brown (1831)

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Double membrane surrounding nucleus; has perinuclear space (10–50 nm); outer membrane continuous with RER

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Opening in nuclear envelope where two membranes fuse; passage for RNA and protein between nucleus and cytoplasm

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Fluid inside nucleus; contains nucleolus and chromatin

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Spherical non-membrane body in nucleoplasm; site of rRNA synthesis; larger in cells active in protein synthesis

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Nucleoprotein fibre in interphase nucleus; DNA + histone proteins + non-histone proteins + RNA; condenses into chromosomes during division

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Condensed chromatin visible during cell division; contains genes; has centromere and two chromatids

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Primary constriction on chromosome; point of spindle fibre attachment; holds two chromatids

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Chromosome with centromere at middle; two equal arms

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Chromosome with centromere slightly off-centre; one shorter and one longer arm

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Chromosome with centromere near one end; one very short and one very long arm

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Chromosome with terminal centromere; one arm only

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Small fragment-like region on chromosome due to secondary constriction; non-staining region

Chapter: Ch8 Cell: The Unit of Life
Definition: Small membrane-bound vesicle containing enzymes; e.g., peroxisomes; present in both plant and animal cells
Carbon compound found in living organisms; includes both small molecules (<1000 Da) and macromolecules
Biomolecule with identified function in normal physiology; e.g., amino acids, sugars, fatty acids, nucleotides
Compound in plants/fungi/microbes beyond primary metabolites; e.g., alkaloids, rubber, essential oils, antibiotics, pigments
Large polymer biomolecule in acid-insoluble fraction; proteins, nucleic acids, polysaccharides; MW > 10,000 Da
Building block of proteins; has amino group (–NH2), carboxyl group (–COOH) and R group on α-carbon; 20 types in proteins
Amino acid that body cannot synthesise; must be obtained from diet; e.g., leucine, lysine, tryptophan
Amino acid form with both –NH3+ and –COO- groups; net charge zero; in solution at isoelectric pH
Carboxyl group attached to hydrocarbon R group; saturated (no double bonds) or unsaturated (with C=C)
Fatty acid with no C=C double bonds; e.g., palmitic acid (C16), stearic acid (C18)
Fatty acid with one or more C=C double bonds; e.g., arachidonic acid (C20, 4 double bonds)
Trihydroxy propane; backbone of fats and oils; esterified with fatty acids to form triglycerides
Three fatty acids esterified to glycerol; main storage lipid (fats at room temp, oils if liquid)
Lipid with glycerol + two fatty acids + phosphorylated organic compound (e.g., choline); main component of cell membrane; e.g., lecithin
Heterocyclic nitrogen-containing compound in nucleotides; purines (adenine, guanine) and pyrimidines (cytosine, thymine, uracil)
Double-ring nitrogenous base; adenine (A) and guanine (G); in both DNA and RNA
Single-ring nitrogenous base; cytosine (C), thymine (T, in DNA), uracil (U, in RNA)
Nitrogenous base + sugar (ribose or deoxyribose); e.g., adenosine, thymidine, uridine, cytidine, guanosine
Nitrogenous base + sugar + phosphate; building block of nucleic acids; e.g., adenylic acid (AMP)
Polymer of monosaccharides; e.g., cellulose, starch, glycogen, chitin, inulin
Homopolymer of glucose; structural component of plant cell wall; cannot be digested by humans
Storage polysaccharide in plants; homopolymer of glucose; forms helix that holds I2 (turns blue)
Storage polysaccharide in animals; branched homopolymer of glucose; in liver and muscle
Complex polysaccharide of N-acetylglucosamine; forms exoskeleton of arthropods and cell wall of fungi
Storage polysaccharide; polymer of fructose; found in dahlia tubers
Polypeptide or polymer of amino acids linked by peptide bonds; heteropolymer of 20 amino acid types; structural and functional roles
Covalent bond between carboxyl group of one amino acid and amino group of next; links amino acids in protein chain
Linear sequence of amino acids in polypeptide chain; N-terminal to C-terminal end
Local folding pattern of polypeptide chain; α-helix (right-handed) and β-pleated sheet; stabilised by hydrogen bonds
Right-handed helical secondary structure of protein; stabilised by hydrogen bonds between backbone NH and CO groups
Flat secondary structure of protein; polypeptide strands side by side with H-bonds; parallel or antiparallel
Overall 3D folding of entire polypeptide chain; formed by interactions of R groups; gives functional shape
Arrangement of multiple polypeptide subunits relative to each other; e.g., haemoglobin (2α + 2β subunits)
Most abundant protein in animal kingdom; structural protein; forms intercellular ground substance
Protein catalyst that accelerates biological reactions; lowers activation energy; substrate-specific
Nucleic acid (RNA) with catalytic activity; not a protein; discovered by Altman and Cech
Crevice or pocket in enzyme where substrate binds; complementary in shape to substrate
Molecule that binds to enzyme active site and is converted to product (S→P)
Transient intermediate formed when substrate binds to enzyme active site (ES complex); essential for catalysis
Energy required to break substrate bonds and reach transition state; enzymes lower this barrier
Temperature at which enzyme shows maximum activity; above it enzyme is denatured
pH at which enzyme shows maximum activity; deviation reduces activity
Maximum velocity of enzyme reaction; reached when all enzyme molecules are saturated with substrate
Molecule structurally similar to substrate; competes for active site; reduces enzyme activity; e.g., malonate inhibits succinic dehydrogenase
Non-protein component bound to enzyme making it catalytically active; prosthetic group, coenzyme or metal ion
Protein portion of enzyme without its cofactor; inactive by itself
Tightly bound organic cofactor; part of active site; e.g., haem in peroxidase and catalase
Loosely bound organic cofactor; transiently associates with enzyme; often vitamin derivative; e.g., NAD, NADP
Complete, catalytically active enzyme with apoenzyme + cofactor
Series of enzyme-catalysed sequential reactions converting one molecule to another; e.g., glycolysis (glucose → pyruvate)
Enzyme class catalysing oxidation-reduction reactions; includes dehydrogenases
Enzyme class catalysing transfer of a functional group from one substrate to another
Enzyme class catalysing hydrolysis of bonds (ester, peptide, glycosidic, etc.)
Enzyme class catalysing removal of groups leaving double bonds (non-hydrolytic)
Enzyme class catalysing interconversion of optical, geometric or positional isomers
Enzyme class catalysing joining of two compounds with ATP hydrolysis; forms C-O, C-S, C-N, P-O bonds

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Ordered sequence of events by which a cell duplicates its genome and divides into two daughter cells; interphase + M phase

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Preparatory phase between two M phases; includes G1 + S + G2; >95% of cell cycle duration; cell grows and DNA replicates

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Gap 1: period between mitosis and S phase; cell grows metabolically; no DNA replication; proteins synthesised

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Synthesis phase; DNA replication occurs; DNA amount doubles (2C → 4C); chromosome number unchanged; centrioles duplicate

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Gap 2: after S phase; cell continues to grow; proteins for mitosis synthesised; lasts until M phase begins

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Quiescent stage; cells exit G1 and stop dividing; metabolically active but non-proliferating; e.g., heart cells, neurons

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Mitosis phase: nuclear division (karyokinesis) + cytoplasmic division (cytokinesis); produces two daughter cells

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Equational division; produces two genetically identical diploid daughter cells; four stages: prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Division of the nucleus; includes prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Division of cytoplasm after karyokinesis; in animals by cleavage furrow; in plants by cell plate formation

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: First stage of mitosis; chromosomes condense, centrosomes move to poles, asters form, spindle appears, nuclear envelope and nucleolus disappear

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Second stage; chromosomes maximally condensed; align at metaphase plate; kinetochores attach to spindle fibres from both poles; best stage to study chromosome morphology

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Third stage; centromeres split; chromatids (now called chromosomes) move to opposite poles; centromere leads

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Final stage; chromosomes decondense; nuclear envelope and nucleolus reform; two daughter nuclei formed

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Imaginary equatorial plane at cell centre where chromosomes align during metaphase

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Array of microtubules radiating from centrosome during mitosis; forms part of mitotic apparatus

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Microtubule of mitotic spindle; connects centrosome to kinetochores (chromosomal) or to opposite pole (polar)

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: New cell wall precursor forming in centre of plant cell during cytokinesis; grows outward from Golgi vesicles; becomes middle lamella

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Inward pinching of plasma membrane during animal cell cytokinesis; deepens until cells are separated

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Multinucleate cell resulting from karyokinesis without cytokinesis; e.g., liquid endosperm of coconut

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Reductive division; one diploid cell → four haploid cells; includes meiosis I and meiosis II; occurs during gametogenesis

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: First meiotic division; homologous chromosomes separate; reduces chromosome number by half; includes Prophase I with 5 sub-stages

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Second meiotic division; sister chromatids separate; resembles mitosis; no DNA replication between meiosis I and II

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: First stage of Prophase I; chromosomes start becoming visible; compaction begins

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Second stage of Prophase I; homologous chromosomes pair (synapsis); synaptonemal complex forms; bivalents (tetrads) appear

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Pairing of homologous chromosomes during zygotene; accompanied by formation of synaptonemal complex

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Protein scaffold holding synapsed homologous chromosomes together during zygotene; site of recombination

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Pair of synapsed homologous chromosomes (= tetrad); consists of four chromatids; clearly visible in pachytene

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Third stage of Prophase I; tetrads distinct; crossing over occurs between non-sister chromatids at recombination nodules

Chapter: Ch10 Cell Cycle and Cell Division
Definition: Sites on bivalent chromosomes where crossing over occurs during pachytene
